region.text: Kumasi and the Asante states round it, Cliopatria's 1702 shape (the keyframe of 1701), not the whole Ashanti region

ledger.note: 1701: Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye's coalition of Asante states defeats Denkyira at Feyiase. 'In 1701, Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye led a coalition of Asante states against Denkyira' and 'defeated them at the Battle of Feyiase'; infobox 'Established: 1670/1701'. The page gives Kumasi, not a boundary. [fx-44, R079: the region 'Ashanti' held 333 cells, 173 of them outside Cliopatria's 1702 shape (Bono's Brong Ahafo among them), which the ashanti-empire_1701 keyframe snap (177 cells) then released to nobody; it is now Cliopatria's 1702 shape. Bono page: 'Asante invaded Bono in 1722-1723' and 'Bono was defeated in 1723, ending its independence', so Bono is the 1722 gain (ledger 2), not land of 1701.]

region.text: Ahafo, formerly Aowin territory

ledger.note: 1722: the Ashanti defeat Aowin and claim Ahafo (1719-1722). 'The Ashanti defeated the Aowin and claimed Ahafo, which had been Aowin territory.'

region.text: the Bono state and Techiman (Takyiman)

ledger.note: 1722: Bono is conquered. 'In 1722, Bono was conquered by subterfuge using Bafo Pim and the Nkoronzas.' The Opoku Ware page dates the invasion 1723-1724, 'which made Bono part of the empire', and the conquest of Techiman 'in the early 18th century'.

region.text: Wassa, in the south-west

ledger.note: 1726: the Ashanti invade Wassa. 'In 1726, the Ashanti invaded Wassa, and its king moved his capital to Abrade near the coast'; 'By 1726, Asante was ready to deal with Wassa, now ruled by Intsiful Asare', who attacked in 1729. The Ashanti page lists Wassa as a tributary without a date, so the start of the tributary tint is the researcher's bridge.

region.text: Gyaman, round Bondoukou

ledger.note: 1732: the Ashanti invade Western Gonja and Gyaman. 'In 1732, the Ashanti invaded Western Gonja and Gyaman'; the Ashanti page names Gyaman and Dagomba among the tributaries.

region.text: Gonja, in the north-west of the Northern region

ledger.note: 1732: Western Gonja falls under Ashanti. 'In 1732, the Ashanti invaded Western Gonja and Gyaman'; Eastern Gonja is absorbed by 1744.

region.text: Banda, in the west of Brong-Ahafo

ledger.note: 1740: the Ashanti invade Banda. 'In 1740, the Ashanti invaded Banda'; the Osei Kwadwo page has Banda 'subjugated in the third attack' (undated).

region.text: Akyem Abuakwa and Kotoku

ledger.note: 1742: Akyem Abuakwa and Kotoku are incorporated. 'In 1742, the Ashanti incorporated the Akyem states of Abuakwa and Kotoku.' The Osei Kwadwo page has Akyem Abuakwa conquered in 1765, and 'In 1742 war broke out again between Asante and Akyem' (Ashanti page).

region.text: Accra and the coastal towns to its east

ledger.note: 1742: Accra and the coast east of it accept Ashanti overrule. 'The Ashanti occupied Accra and the coastal towns to its east. The Ga-Adangbe accepted Ashanti overrule but won an exemption from tribute'; the Dutch then 'paid a stipend for the fort and land at Accra'.

region.text: Eastern Gonja and Dagbon (Dagomba), the north of the Northern region

ledger.note: 1744: Eastern Gonja is absorbed and Dagbon conquered. 'By 1744, Eastern Gonja was absorbed'; '1744-1745: The conquest of Dagbon (Dagomba)'. The Ashanti page puts Dagomba in 'the early 1770s' and the Osei Kwadwo page (c. 1772) is unsure whether the force sent to Dagbon conquered or negotiated.

region.text: Akyem Abuakwa

ledger.note: 1765: Osei Kwadwo conquers Akyem Abuakwa. 'In June 1765 he waged war on the coastal alliance. Akyem was defeated and Akyem Abuakwa was conquered into the Ashanti Empire.' Replaced its ruler in 1772.

region.text: the Fante country on the coast

ledger.note: 1816: the Fante are absorbed. 'In 1806, Asante forces pursued two rebel leaders through Fante territory to the coast. In 1807, disputes led to the Ashanti-Fante War. By 1816, Asante had absorbed the Fante Confederacy.' The Anglo-Ashanti page adds that after the Ashanti-Akim-Akwapim War (1814-16) the African Company of Merchants signed a friendship treaty recognising Ashanti sovereignty over much of the coast, and lists a 1817 'perpetual peace and harmony' treaty with Osei Bonsu.

region.text: Accra and the coast east of it

ledger.note: 1826: the Ashanti are beaten at Dodowa. 'Battle of Dodowa, 7 Aug 1826: British victory. Congreve rockets caused the Ashanti to fall back.' The page does not say Accra was given up; the end of the Ga-Adangbe tributary tint is dated here and the 1831 treaty fixes the Pra border.

region.text: the coast and Assin country south of the Pra: 'the Pra River accepted as the border' (1831 treaty); Assin, Akim, Adanse and Denkyira claims renounced at Fomena (1874)

ledger.note: 1831: the Pra River becomes the border. 'In 1831, a treaty led to 30 years of peace, with the Pra River accepted as the border' (the Ashanti page has the same sentence). The land south of the Pra, the Fante coast and Assin, is read as Central region.

region.text: the coast round Elmina and Cape Coast

ledger.note: 1873: the last Ashanti invasion of the coast. 'In 1872 Britain bought the Dutch Gold Coast, including Elmina, which the Ashanti claimed. This triggered the invasion of the new British protectorate' (Third Anglo-Ashanti War, 1873-1875); the British colony page: Asante made 'their last invasion of the coast in 1873'.

region.text: the coast round Elmina and Cape Coast

ledger.note: 1874: Kumasi is taken and the Treaty of Fomena ends the war. The British took Kumasi on 4 February 1874; the treaty 'was formed sometime in February of 1874', on 13 February (the Anglo-Ashanti page says it was signed in July 1874).

region.text: Assin, Akim, Adanse and Denkyira

ledger.note: 1874: Fomena. The Ashanti 'gave up claims to Assin, Akim, Adanse, and Denkyira' and to Elmina; the page 'does not say these were formally lost'. Read as the loss of the tributary south and east of Kumasi.

region.text: Brong, which 'became independent as a result of the treaty and the British victory' (Fomena, 1874)

ledger.note: 1874: Brong becomes independent. 'Brong, Gonja, and Dagomba became independent as a result of the treaty and the British victory.'

region.text: Gonja and Dagbon

ledger.note: 1874: Gonja and Dagbon become independent (see the Brong entry).

region.text: Gonja and Dagbon

ledger.note: 1874: Dagbon (Dagomba) becomes independent (see the Brong entry).

region.text: Wassa, in the south-west

ledger.note: 1874: the Ashanti 'agreed to withdraw troops from the South-West and other places' (Fomena page); read as the end of the Wassa tributary tint, the page does not name Wassa.

region.text: Gyaman, round Bondoukou

ledger.note: 1895: the Ivory Coast part of Cliopatria's shape disappears; no page opened gives a date or a cause for Gyaman, so this is the researcher's bridge to the Cliopatria shape.

region.text: the Ashanti state and its tributaries

ledger.note: 1896: the British occupy Kumasi and end the Ashanti state. Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War (26 December 1895 to 4 February 1896): 'Kumasi was entered in January 1896, and Prempeh I was deposed and exiled. A protection treaty was imposed.' The British colony page: 'In 1896, the British forced Asante to become a protectorate'. The Anglo-Ashanti page dates the protectorate 1897; the colony came on 26 September 1901 and 'the Asante empire became part of the Gold Coast colony on 1 January 1902'.

wars.name: Battle of Feyiase
wars.outcome: The Asante coalition under Osei Tutu defeated Denkyira, ending its overlordship; the Dutch began paying their Elmina tribute to the Ashanti instead (Dutch Gold Coast page).

wars.name: Ashanti conquests under Opoku Ware I
wars.outcome: Aowin and Bono incorporated (1719-1724), Wassa invaded (1726), Western Gonja and Gyaman invaded (1732), Banda (1740), the Akyem states and Accra (1742), Eastern Gonja (by 1744), Dagbon (1744-45).

wars.name: Battle of Atakpame
wars.outcome: Ashanti defeated by Oyo and Dahomey; the Dwaben-hene was lost and Kusi Obodom removed; no loss of territory recorded.
wars.note: The Osei Kwadwo page links a 'Battle of Atakpame' page but does not describe the battle or its site; the Togo hills later a 'neutral zone between Ashanti and Dahomey' (Wilks, undated).

wars.name: Ashanti-Fante War
wars.outcome: The British refused to hand over two rebels the Ashanti had pursued to the coast; one was handed over; by 1816 the Ashanti had absorbed the Fante Confederacy.

wars.name: Ashanti-Akim-Akwapim War
wars.outcome: The Ashanti defeated the Akim-Akwapim alliance; the African Company of Merchants then signed a friendship treaty recognising Ashanti sovereignty over much of the coast.

wars.name: First Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: Ashanti victory at Nsamankow (January 1824, MacCarthy killed); British victory at Dodowa (7 August 1826); the Pra River became the border in 1831.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: British victory; Kumasi occupied on 4 February 1874 and the Treaty of Fomena signed in February 1874 (the Anglo-Ashanti page: July): indemnity of 50,000 ounces of gold, claims on Assin, Akim, Adanse, Denkyira and Elmina renounced.
wars.note: The Anglo-Ashanti page gives 1873-1875 for the war.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: British victory: Kumasi entered in January 1896, Prempeh I deposed and exiled, a protection treaty imposed; the state ends in 1896.
wars.note: 26 December 1895 to 4 February 1896. The War of the Golden Stool (28 March to September 1900) and the Ashanti Crown Colony (26 September 1901) fall after the state's end.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the shapes are envelopes of the core and its tributaries (Banda, Gyaman, Gonja and Dagbon are tributary tint, not drawn).
The southern frontier is the Pra River after 1831 and the Fomena treaty of 1874 fixes the loss of claims, but no survey line is given; the northern and western frontiers stay soft.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW. Starts 1702 (page: 1701; infobox 1670/1701) and runs to 1897 (page: the state ends in 1896 with Kumasi's occupation, the protectorate and Prempeh's exile; 1897 is the Anglo-Ashanti page's protectorate date; 1902 the infobox end). The outline is an envelope: 1744 onward it reaches the sea at about 5 N (56 cells) and Ivory Coast, and keeps the same 153,000-154,000 km2 from 1769 to 1894. Three kinds of correction: (1) 1757-1768 Togo cells removed on the Osei Kwadwo page's 'neutral zone' sentence (weak); (2) 1836-1872 Central region removed because the 1831 treaty made the Pra the border; (3) 1874-1895 Fomena losses (Central, Eastern, Adanse, Brong). The Ivory Coast part disappears in 1895 with no page opened (unverified: page budget). Vassal tint (Wassa, Gyaman, Gonja, Dagbon, Ga-Adangbe) is the reading of the Ashanti article's 'tributaries: Wassa, Twifo, Gyaman, Dagomba' and of the Opoku Ware page's conquest dates. DISAGREEMENTS. Bono 1722 (Ashanti page) vs 1723-24 (Opoku Ware); Akyem 1742 vs 1765; Dagbon 1744-45 vs c. 1772 vs 'early 1770s'; Fomena February 1874 (Fomena page, signed 13 February) vs July 1874 (Anglo-Ashanti page); war end 1875 vs 1874; Osei Kwadwo died 1777 or 1778; protectorate 1896 vs 1897. NOT FOUND ON THE PAGES: the Dutch tribute for Elmina is on the Dutch Gold Coast page (two ounces of gold a month from 1701, the 'Elmina Note' questioned), not on the Ashanti pages; Akwamu, Akuapim and Sehwi submitted 'at the end of the reign' of Osei Kwadwo (1777), undated, so no event; Twifo and Denkyira after 1701; Juaben/Dwaben secession after 1874. RULERS. Only Osei Tutu I (c. 1695-1717), Opoku Ware I (c. 1720-1750) and Osei Kwadwo (1764-1777) have years on the pages, so no ruler strip. COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Denkyira (af-04-x), Akwamu, Wassa, Gyaman, Bono (Takyiman), Gonja, Dagbon, Akyem Abuakwa, Fante Confederacy, Aowin, Banda. The British Gold Coast row starts in 1873, so the Fante coast under British protection 1821-1872 has no polity.
